title: Linear mixing keeps VISp-axis variances fixed while it steepens spectra in paired stimulus models
abstract: We test whether higher-area spectral compression outside dominant VISp axes requires signals outside the VISp span. Exact paired response models keep every VISp-axis variance fixed while an invertible linear map steepens target spectra. Rank-40 models match three saved natural-stimulus hierarchy slopes by design. The VISp-axis slope is zero and a fixed higher-area basis recovers a positive slope. Maximum map gains are 1.16 to 1.22. A designed weak-tail extension has rank 117 without changing the fitted ranks. The effect reverses for some other source ranks, so it is not a universal mixing rule. We apply the established operator factorization theorem to a full-kernel gain test. We prove sharp minimum trace, operator norm and rank budgets for unrecorded source signals at a fixed readout gain. Independent-repeat simulations check a directional witness; shared repeat noise biases it. These are exact model and method results, not a fit to Allen response matrices or evidence for a circuit mechanism. No new animals enter the study. Original code, one licensed aggregate calibration table, proofs, model outputs and reproduction steps are included.
